main_text.p: nũs[?] docet, locum in urbe peramplum fuisse moenibus contiguum, cui nomen Megara, & eum, occupatâ prius privati hominis turri sitâ extra moenia iisdem moenibus proximâ, & paris cum moenibus altitudinis, ex eadem illa turri per noctem oppugnatum & captum esse à Scipione, atque istuc ipsum, diffractâ per audaces juvenes, qui primi ex moenibus in Megara desilierant, portâ, cum militibus quater mille ingressum, ac in tantum terrorem tum Carthaginienses dedisse, ut hi quasi reliqua urbe captâ in Byrsam arcem confugerint: verum Scipionem, propterea quòd Megara hortis & stirpibus æstivorum fructuum feracibus plena essent, & maceriis vivisque sepibus ac aliis sentibus di-stincta,& rivi profundi ac flexuosi complures quoque locum permearent, insidias nocturnas tali loco veritum, si sui hostem persequerentur, pedem inde tunc retulisse. Dein paulò post Appianus hæc addit: Scipio toto Isthmo (intelligit cervicem, quâ Carthaginis sedes seu solum peninsulare continenti collaterebat) potitus fossam a mari ad mare perduxit, ad teli iactum ab hostibus sf-motus. Illi tamen opus impedire conabantur, quod per stadia xxv militibus operantibus simul & propugnantibus ab-solutum

page.notes: Show-through and stains at the bottom left (fragments of text from the reverse side) are not transcribed. The first word "nūs" is a fragment from the previous line and carries a doubtful macron; marked [?]. The printed hyphen in "sf-motus" is a typographic line-end break (sfmotus, i.e. "ab hostibus sefmotus" in the printer's hyphenated form) and is transcribed as printed; the word appears as "sfmotus" with a long s rendered as f in print, so the exact letters are uncertain. Italic and roman segments are as seen; the parenthesis is set in roman.
